semantic_contract: 0x00c70150 answers a yes/no question about a simulation owner: is there at least one entry that is currently usable? It takes the owner object plus a key source and a strictness flag, and proceeds in four stages. Stage one is a hard gate: if the owner's dword at +0x194 is not 5 the answer is immediately no and nothing else is touched. Stage two walks the owner's list, whose length is (dword[+0x160] - dword[+0x15c]) >> 2, and for each element compares the element's dword at +0x14 against the key source's dword at +0x84; a mismatch advances to the next element. Stage three, for a matching element only, walks that element's own list at +0x3c/+0x40 and applies one of two acceptance rules depending on the strict flag: a zero flag accepts the very first element of the list without inspecting it, while a non-zero flag requires at least one element whose remaining count, computed as dword[+0x24] minus the population count of the byte mask at +0x28, is greater than one. An empty inner list can never accept, so the strict rule requires a list with at least one element that has two or more charges left. Stage four is the fallback, reached only when the scan found nothing: if the space-player flag read through 0x01021080 is non-zero the answer is no, and otherwise the "Simulator/SimSingleton" service is created on demand (200 bytes, registered under that name), its queue at +0x28 is tested for emptiness, and a non-empty queue yields yes. The function returns a single byte, writes no receiver field, and mutates exactly one piece of global state: the cached singleton pointer. Its only permanent side effect is therefore the lazy creation of that singleton.
classification_rationale: The complete 259-byte body, all 96 instructions, both nested loops, every field offset, every immediate, the global, the registration string, both fallback callees in full, and every branch polarity are read directly from the disassembly and corroborated by ten call sites plus a fully inlined analogue at 0x00c61a93. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for three named bounds. First, an ABI discrepancy: the body reads a fourth stack slot at 0x00c701d0 that no inspected caller writes, so the argument count is either three with an uninitialised read or four with callers that were not found; the reconstruction models it as a fourth cdecl parameter and says so. Second, the class of argument 1 is not established: no RTTI exists, no vtable was located, and the +0x15c/+0x160/+0x194 offset signature matches no ModAPI declaration. Third, the semantics of the acceptance test are bounded by the meanings of the operands rather than by their mechanics: the kind value 5 at +0x194, the key at +0x84 and the capacity pair at +0x24/+0x28 are all observed as reads and comparisons but never observed being written, so what they denote is inferred from the shape alone. The control flow, the memory behaviour and the frame arithmetic carry no residual uncertainty.
semantic_findings: The function is a two-level existence test with a lazy-service fallback: scan the owner's list for a key match, then that match's own list for a usable charge, and if nothing matches ask the SimSingleton queue instead.

The strict flag inverts the inner rule rather than tightening it: zero accepts the first element unconditionally, non-zero requires a remaining count above one. Both modes are reachable and both are used, with 0x00c35887, 0x00c35144, 0x00c61a34, 0x00c61b5a and 0x00c630b7 passing zero and 0x00c70b3a and 0x01068b6a passing a caller-supplied value.
0x00ff0870 is a remaining-capacity computation, dword[+0x24] minus popcount(byte[+0x28]), not a bit index. The Ghidra decompiler's SWAR expression is correct but its apparent bit-scan reading is not.
The space-player gate at 0x00c70203 has inverted polarity: a non-zero flag produces no, so the fallback only runs in the non-space case.
The SimSingleton store at 0x00c70233 is redundant: 0x00ae5c30 already writes 0x0167a60c from inside its own constructor, so the store publishes the same pointer twice.
The allocation-failure path stores an explicit 0 at 0x00c70231/0x00c70233, so the global is never left holding a partially constructed object.

The first argument slot is reused as the outer loop counter, which is why the reload at 0x00c70190 sits on the loop back edge rather than at the loop head, and why argument 2 is reloaded on every iteration yet never used.

An inlined copy of both loops exists at 0x00c61a93..0x00c61b22 with the same callee triple and the same vector layout but a magic-constant acceptance test (0x18ea2cc at 0x00c61af0), which is direct evidence that the loop shape is a shared idiom rather than a one-off.

The owner object passed as argument 1 is itself reached through a +0x13c field of the caller's object (0x00c70b2d, 0x00c61a25), so the same list is addressed through two levels of indirection in different callers.
unresolved_questions: The binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so no class identity can be read from typeinfo; class claims in this record rest only on observed vtable data and SDK header text.
No original-process trace exists for any function in this batch. Every statement here is static.

How many stack arguments does 0x00c70150 really take? The body reads a fourth slot at ESP0+0x10 (0x00c701d0) but all ten inspected call sites push three words and clean twelve bytes. Either a caller that pushes four was not found, or the read is of an uninitialised slot whose observed value happens to be zero.

If the fourth slot is uninitialised, what is its value at run time, and does the non-strict accept branch therefore execute by accident at some call sites? This changes the meaning of eight of the ten observed call sites.
What class owns argument 1? The +0x15c/+0x160 list, the +0x194 kind and the +0x14c/+0x150 text buffer are observed, but nothing identifies the type.

What is the kind value 5? 0x00c47cc0 reaches an App::IAppSystem::Init transition when the mode field at +0x84 equals 3, so the receiver carries both a mode and a kind; the enum behind +0x194 is not in any ModAPI header.

What is the key at argument_3->[0x84] and the key at element->[0x14]? Both are only ever compared. 0x00c451e0 in the callers returns the object at this->+0x90, resolved lazily from an id at +0x8c, which suggests a resource or prototype id, but that is inference and is not claimed.

What do the +0x24 total and the +0x28 mask of an inner element mean? dword[+0x24] minus popcount(byte[+0x28]) is a remaining count, and the acceptance threshold is strictly greater than one, but neither the writer of those fields nor their unit was located.

Why does the inlined analogue at 0x00c61a93 use the magic constant 0x18ea2cc where the out-of-line version consults the strict flag? The two are not obviously the same predicate, and the analogue additionally calls 0x00ff0760 at 0x00c61b07, which 0x00c70150 never does.

What is 0x00c451e0, called at 0x00c61a2d and 0x00c61b53 to build argument 2? Its body resolves this->+0x90 from the id at +0x8c through 0x00b3d2a0 and 0x00ba9370, with a virtual call at slot 0 and slot +0x4 on the old value, but its role is not established.
Three of the ten call sites (0x00c308ec, 0x00c34568, 0x00c59711) were not disassembled.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00c70150. The 0x00c701d0 read of an apparently uninitialised stack slot is the single most important runtime gate: a trace must record the flag value at that address on entry to each of the ten call sites.
A runtime differential test must confirm the owner's +0x194 value is 5 whenever the scan is expected to run, since a different value would make every call return 0.
The 0x00c70221 ADD ESP,0x18 and the 0x00f473a0 argument order must be observed live to confirm the six-argument allocation contract.
The population-count computation in 0x00ff0870 must be checked against a live element, because the acceptance threshold of 1 depends on its exact result.
